explanation: Painters used oil-based paint long before him, including in 7th-century Buddhist cave murals at Bamiyan, Afghanistan. Van Eyck perfected oil glazes, and the 16th-century writer Vasari gave him the credit.

claims.text: Jan van Eyck did not invent oil painting; oil-based paints were in use centuries earlier.
Oil-based paints were used in 7th-century Buddhist cave murals at Bamiyan in Afghanistan.
Jan van Eyck refined the technique of painting in oil glazes.
In the 16th century Giorgio Vasari credited Jan van Eyck with inventing oil painting.
